recommendation: Re-base the effect assumptions on benchmarks
detail: Plan on placebo remission of 11-13% and 600 mg remission of about 20-30%, not 40%. Present the 40% case as the optimistic scenario.
impact: Shows the real risk: power at benchmark rates is about 18%, not 83%.

recommendation: Use clinical response on the modified Mayo score as the primary proof-of-concept endpoint
detail: Keep remission as the key secondary. Response has a larger, more stable signal in phase 2 and matches the regulators' modified Mayo score.
impact: At the same 90 patients, power rises from 26% to 36% (benchmark rates, chi-square approximation).

recommendation: Concentrate patients on the dose most likely to work
detail: Drop the 300 mg arm, or add it only through an adaptive dose-selection step after an interim look.
impact: With 45 vs 45, response power rises to 48%.

recommendation: Size the trial for a realistic effect
detail: Two arms of about 80 patients each, with a pre-specified one-sided α of 0.10 for proof of concept.
impact: Gives about 80% power on clinical response at benchmark rates (chi-square approximation).

recommendation: Add an interim futility look at 50% of patients
detail: Run by an independent statistician for an unblinded data monitoring committee; stop if conditional power is below 20%.
impact: If the drug does nothing, about 75% of trials stop at halfway, sparing patients. The cost is small: power falls from 50% to 45% at a realistic effect, and from 99% to 98% at the protocol's assumption (80 per arm).

recommendation: Match the sample-size method to the analysis and pre-specify Firth or exact logistic regression
detail: Compute power for the adjusted logistic model actually used, and fix the 70% pooled-power text.
impact: Removes the analysis failure seen in 8% of simulated trials.

detail: Keep central reading and the endoscopy subscore of 2 or more; consider a higher entry bar (full Mayo 6 or more) and avoid adding visits beyond what the endpoints need.
impact: Each extra point of placebo response costs power; at 15% placebo the planned design falls to about 56%.

detail: Plan retention support and rescue rules so patients stay in follow-up; dropouts count as failures.
impact: Under protocol assumptions power goes from 80% at 10% dropout to 66% at 30%.

recommendation: Pre-set safety review triggers for IL-6 class risks
detail: An unblinded committee reviews at once for any gastrointestinal perforation or abscess, and at pre-set counts of serious infection, low neutrophils or liver-enzyme rises (see checkpoints).
impact: For example, 4 serious infections among 40 patients on active drug means at least 90% probability the true rate is above 5%.
